newsitem.title: DUBAI: SOCCER-SAUDI ARABIA CRUSH 10-MAN THAILAND 6-0 IN ASIAN CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SAUDI ARABIA CRUSH 10-MAN THAILAND 6-0 IN ASIAN CUP.

text.p: Saudi Arabia cruised to a 6-0 win in their Group B match at the Asian Cup on Thursday after Thailand had goalkeeper Wacharapong Somcit sent off only nine minutes into the match.
Wacharapong was given his marching orders for bringing down Ibrahim Al Harbi as the Saudi player was rounding him. Khaled Al Temawi converted the spot kick and the Saudis never looked back.
Striker Fahad Mahalel made it 2-0 in the 15th minute, heading home after substitute keeper Nipon Malanont failed to hold a shot by Khaled Al Mowalad.
Mowalad increased the Saudi lead three minutes later, hitting a low shot into Nipon's left corner from 12 metres out.
The Egyptian referee awarded Saudi Arabia a second penalty in the 29th minute when Pathanapang Sripramote brought down Sami Al Jaber. Temawi again beat Nipon to make it 4-0.
The Saudis repeatedly tore apart the Thai defence, coming close on several occasions and hitting the post before Jaber volleyed home a cross from the right in the 52nd minutes.
Two minutes later Mahalel made space for himself inside the box and beat Nipon with a fierce drive to score his second and Saudi Arabia's sixth.
Despite their healthy lead the Saudis never relaxed their attacking play, hitting the woodwork twice more and forcing a string of fine saves from Thailand's substitute keeper.

Saudi Arabia: 1-Mohammed al-Deayea, 2-Mohammed Al Jahani, 3-Mohammed Khilaiwi, 4-Abdullah Zubromawi, 8-Khaled Al Temawi (24-Khamis Al Zahrani 71), 9-Sami Al Jaber (6-Fuad Amin 60), 10- Fahad Mahalel, 12-Ibrahim Al Harbi, 13-Hussein Sulimani, 14- Khaled Al Mowalad, 16-Khamis Al Dossary (25-Abdullah Aldosary 60).

Thailand: 1-Wacharapong Somcit, 2-Kritsada Piandit, 4- Phathanapang Sripramote, 6-Sanor Longsawang, 7-Natee Tongsukkao, 8-Apichad Thaveechalermdit, 9-Natipong Sritong-In, 12-Surachai Jaturapattarapong (18-Nipon Malanont 9), 13-Kiatisuk Senamuang, 17-Dusit Chalermsan, 19-Surachai Jirasirichote.
